claims.text: According to OC 186A, UPI Tap & Pay transactions on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must ensure explicit User consent is obtained for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with Users having the ability to opt out at any time.
UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions using UPI Tap & Pay.
Device lock must be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device shall be in an unlocked state at the time of initiating a transaction.
UPI Tap & Pay functionality shall be presented as a standalone feature through a dedicated call-to-action and shall not be embedded within any other service, feature, or menu category.

sources.text: fs Conroe =) NPCI/UPI/OC no.199/2024-25 25" June 2024 To, All Members, UPI (Unified Payment Interface) Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above UPI has become a preferred digital payment mode across the country. It provides ease of use, convenience and superior user experience with security and interoperability. To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. There are security checks implemented as part of the code embedded in the Common Library (CL) along with the feature release to enhance user experience on UPI platforms. Integration of latest versions of CL is important to ensure enhanced security and safety in UPI ecosystem. With this objective, NPCI will be retiring the support for CL prior to Version 1.8 after 30% September 2024. To ensure compliance PSP Banks shall certify and enable CL 1.8 or above and their respective UPI Apps shall integrate the latest version of CL within their application, on or before 30% September 2024. Members are requested to take note of this compliance and communicate it to relevant stakeholders and their respective partners. Yours sincerely, SD/- Kunal Kalawatia Chief of Products 1001A, The Capital, B Wing, 10* Floor, Bandra Kurla Complex,
sources.title: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above

sources.text: ander eestr yprart rrr NATIONAL PAYMENTS CORPORATION OF INDIA NPCIUPI/OC No 170/2023-24 20" September 2023 To All Members participating in Unified Payment Interface (UPI) Subject: RBIs Digital Rupee - CBDC and UPI Interoperability RBI's Digital Rupee facilitates fast and efficient transactions, which aims to enhance financial inclusion. It further provides a secure and regulated digital alternative to physical cash. In line with RBI's decision to enhance interoperability between UPI and Digital Rupee, it is intended to extend the benefits of UPI Quick Response Code (QR Code) to the Digital Rupee users. This will enable all the merchants that are already using UPI QR Code to be enabled for receiving payments from Digital Rupee users. Members shall implement the following for enabling interoperability and acceptance of UPI QR Codes for Digital Rupee transactions:
